
### going the distance 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/routing-bgp/texfig/distance-prefs.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Options to route between a network in Japan and in Virginia. The network in Virginia has a direct connection to ISP B in NoVA and the network in Japan to ISP A in Tokyo. Both ISP A and ISP B have sites in Tokyo, Los Angeles, and NoVA."}

![](/routing-bgp/texfig/distance-prefs.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Two routes from Virginia to Tokyo: In one, ISP B hands off traffic to ISP A in NoVA and ISP A sends it across the Pacific; in the other, ISP B sends the traffic across the Pacific and hands it off toISP A in Tokyo."}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .vlow}

does ISP A or ISP B help packets cross the Pacific?

:::


### distance preferences  {.smaller}


* ISP B$\rightarrow$ISP A across the Pacific: 
<hr class="vspace" />
* for ISP B: 

   * cheaper to hand-off packet to ISP A as soon as possible
   * more control over performance if handing off as late as possible

* for ISP A: 

   * cheaper to require ISP B to hand-off packet as late as possible
   * more control over performance if B sends as soon as possible

* maybe part of ISP A and ISP B peering agreement
